title: Light, Health and Wellbeing: Implications from chronobiology for architectural design

findings.antecedent: sunny rooms (in a cardiac intensive care unit)
findings.mechanism: natural light-dark/day-night cycle is important for health and recuperation.
findings.quote: outcomes in a cardiac intensive care unit after a heart attack are better in sunny rooms compared to dull rooms, with lower mortality.

findings.antecedent: brighter rooms (for hospitalised patients with depression)
findings.mechanism: natural light-dark/day-night cycle is important for health and recuperation.
findings.quote: hospitalised patients with depression improved approximately three days faster when admitted to brighter rooms than in rooms receiving less daylight

findings.antecedent: brighter lights (installed on a psychiatric ward)
findings.consequent: duration of hospitalisation for depressed patients
findings.mechanism: structured light exposure - intensity, duration and timing is therapeutic.
findings.quote: installing brighter lights on a psychiatric ward, depressed patients had a three-day-shorter duration of hospitalisation.

findings.antecedent: increasing light intensity (in day-rooms of nursing homes where demented patients spend most of their time)

findings.mechanism: This is the principle of the 'phase response curve', which helps us adjust our endogenous circadian rhythms to environmental time cues.
findings.quote: Light in the morning induces a phase advance (rhythms are shifted to earlier, as in a transmeridian flight east)

findings.mechanism: This is the principle of the 'phase response curve', which helps us adjust our endogenous circadian rhythms to environmental time cues.
findings.quote: in the evening, a phase delay (rhythms are shifted to later, as in a transmeridian flight west).

findings.mechanism: The human species evolved to function with more than one hour of daylight per 24 hours
findings.quote: Although indoor lighting (between 50-300 lux) is perfectly adequate for the visual system, it is near darkness for the circadian system.

findings.antecedent: unnatural lighting patterns (insufficient light during the day and too much light at night)
findings.mechanism: more and more people's working and social lives are disrupted by skewed sleep patterns.

findings.antecedent: natural light-dark/day-night cycle (in extreme medical environments)
findings.quote: a natural light-dark/day-night cycle is important for health and recuperation.

limitations: Lack of clear, detailed design guidelines from chronobiology research.
Insufficient understanding of the specifics of complex dynamic lighting systems for chronobiological effects.
Existing multicolour lighting devices are based on insufficient circadian know-how.
Lighting requirements vary significantly by chronotype and age group, making universal guidelines difficult.
